title: Tackling the Challenges of Adding Pulse-level Support to a Heterogeneous HPCQC Software Stack: MQSS Pulse
problem: Heterogeneous HPC-Quantum Computing (HPCQC) software stacks lack native pulse-level control, limiting quantum program expressiveness and hardware utilization. Pulse-level abstractions (ports, frames, waveforms) are not integrated into standard HPC-QC environments.
motivation: Pulse-level control enables low-level quantum hardware access and optimization, but current HPCQC systems (like MQSS) don't support it. Adding pulse support requires addressing challenges across user interfaces, compilers, intermediate representations, and backend interfaces.
method: MQSS Pulse: Extension of Munich Quantum Software Stack with native pulse-level support. Introduces compiled C/C++ pulse API (avoiding Python overhead), extends LLVM for pulse instructions, uses C-based backend interface for hardware constraints, and designs portable pulse exchange format.
key_novelty: Compiled pulse API for low-level efficiency; LLVM extension for pulse instructions; portable pulse exchange format; end-to-end pulse-aware compilation in HPCQC systems.
contributions: Identification of four key challenges for pulse-level integration (UI, compiler IR, backend interface)
Compiled C/C++ pulse API reducing Python overhead
LLVM support extension for pulse-related instructions
C-based backend interface for hardware constraint queries
Portable exchange format for pulse sequences

metrics.scope: End-to-end pulse compilation and runtime execution

limitations: Quantum hardware constraints vary; portable format may have performance trade-offs; integration with classical HPC workflows requires careful orchestration.
